data.reason: Review of attempt 9 (subagent reviewer on opus, triage 143) confirmed attempt 8's F1 closed and its F2 closed for packages/core/tsconfig.json, and found criteria 1, 2, 4 and 5 met and 3 partly met because of one medium. F1: mutation.source_files keeps only entries starting with packages/core/src, so a slice naming a parent directory or a ./-prefixed path passes the tdd gate with no mutation measurement, while paths.covers lets that slice edit src. F2 (low): the kill check decides coverage with mutation.covers on un-normalised names, a second reader of the SEEN-140 question. F3 (low): mutation_ci.CONFIG_FILES omits tsconfig.base.json, which packages/core/tsconfig.json extends. Ruud decided all three are fixed in this ticket (attempt 10). The triage's fingerprint and slice_files failures were judged benign by the reviewer (only the ticket file, README and journal records changed after check 139; every flagged file is named by an earlier accepted plan). F1 and F2 change harness/mutation.py and harness/gates.py and F3 harness/mutation_ci.py, which is a new plan, so the return goes to solution.

findings.claim: source_files keeps only entries that begin with packages/core/src, so a slice naming a parent directory (packages/core, packages) or a ./-prefixed path is held to no mutation floor, while the edit guard (paths.covers, which normalises and accepts parent directories) lets that slice edit any file under packages/core/src.
findings.failure_scenario: SEEN-019's plan has a slice with files ['packages/core', 'harness/x.py']. The guard allows edits to packages/core/src/fee.ts because paths.covers('packages/core/src/fee.ts', ['packages/core']) is True. At tdd, _require_mutation computes mutation.source_files(['packages/core', ...]) == [] and returns, so the attempt advances with no mutation measurement at all. A slice naming './packages/core/src/fee.ts' gets the same: source_files returns []. Reproduced by the reviewer and again in the session before this return.
findings.rule_candidate: none: a disagreement in meaning between two harness Python functions about which plan entries reach packages/core/src; none of the registry's tools reads the harness's path semantics, and only a unit test of the gate over a parent-directory slice can catch it

findings.claim: The kill check decides plan coverage with mutation.covers on un-normalised plan names, a second reader of the question SEEN-140 assigns to paths.covers alone; attempt 9 avoided the NoSecondReaderTest finding by rewriting a comparison, but the call itself is a reader that test cannot see.
findings.failure_scenario: A slice naming './packages/core/src/fee.ts' cites a Stryker RED killing a mutant in packages/core/src/fee.ts; mutation.covers(['./packages/core/src/fee.ts'], 'packages/core/src/fee.ts') is False and source_files maps nothing, so the gate refuses a RED that paths.covers would place in the slice.

findings.claim: CONFIG_FILES now includes packages/core/tsconfig.json but not tsconfig.base.json, which that file extends and the TypeScript checker therefore also reads, so attempt 8's F2 is closed for one of the two files it describes.
findings.failure_scenario: A pull request enables a stricter compiler flag in tsconfig.base.json and changes packages/core/src/fee.ts. mutation_ci.select returns only src/fee.ts, and the incremental cache keeps results for the other src files taken under the old compiler settings.
